entities.summary: Pope Evaristus was the bishop of Rome from approximately 99/100 to 107/108 CE, marking the transition from the Apostolic Age to the Early Christian period. He was also known as Aristus and is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church, and Oriental Orthodoxy. The exact dates of his papacy are uncertain, and some sources suggest he may have begun as early as 96 CE. Evaristus was the first bishop of Rome to be recognized as such by the Roman Empire, and his papacy is significant because it laid the groundwork for the development of the papacy as a central institution in Christianity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Evaristus' papacy marked a significant turning point in the development of the Christian church, as the Roman Empire officially recognized the bishop of Rome as a separate entity and granted greater autonomy and authority.
